clue.text: British cut (not horse), cured meat and game

indicators.note: the bracketed 'not horse' tells us to drop that letter from the word for cut

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
gammon is cured ham from a pig's hind leg

explanation.surface: A butcher's order: a British cut of meat (no horsemeat, please), some gammon, and some game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not horse)' removes H from HACK, leaving ACK. 'Game' looks like more butcher's produce but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two players moving counters by dice throws.

clue.text: I'm bored travelling round new resort abroad

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the letter for new, enclosing it
letters that are travelling are moving about, so the words I'm bored get rearranged

explanation.surface: A bored holidaymaker complains while travelling round a new resort abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges I'M BORED; 'round' wraps those letters around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Benidorm is a Spanish seaside town on the Costa Blanca, a famous package-holiday destination for Britons.

clue.text: Dude with a diary you put at No. 2 in best-seller list

parts.note: cat is old slang for a man or dude
a log is a diary-style record
U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: the letter standing second in the word best-seller is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone with a diary hopes to reach number two in the best-seller list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at No. 2 in' picks the second letter of 'best-seller', E. 'No. 2' sounds like a chart position but counts letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalogue is an itemised list of goods, books or works.

clue.text: An organised unit and salt get the worse for wear

indicators.note: something worse for wear is battered out of shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A tidy unit and its salt supply both deteriorate with use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the worse for wear' rearranges SALT GET.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology a gestalt is an organised whole perceived as more than the sum of its parts.

clue.text: Bar? Come with me to get smashed in town!

indicators.note: smashed things are broken up, so the letters of these three words are shuffled

explanation.surface: An invitation to the bar to get drunk in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get smashed' rearranges BAR, COME and ME together. 'Smashed' reads as drunk but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Morecambe is a seaside town in Lancashire, in north-west England.

clue.text: Runner in Europe punched by Queen? Do behave!

indicators.note: the river name is struck through by the letter for Queen, which ends up inside it

parts.note: the Oder is a river (a runner) flowing between Germany and Poland
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A European athlete is punched by a queen, who then demands better behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete but is a river; 'punched by' puts R inside ODER.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Order!' is what a chair or speaker calls out to demand proper conduct.

clue.text: Well-informed questions put to an audience

indicators.note: something put to an audience is heard by listeners rather than read

parts.note: whys are questions asking for reasons

explanation.surface: A speaker asks informed questions of the people listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to an audience' signals that WHYS is heard, giving a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise person is knowledgeable and judicious, like someone well-informed.

clue.text: In Australia, go away aboard Trondheim ship

indicators.note: the answer is on board, carried inside the words Trondheim ship

explanation.surface: An Australian tells someone on a Norwegian ship to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' points to letters inside TrondheIM SHIp.
explanation.definitionFit: Imshi is Australian slang, borrowed from Arabic by soldiers, for 'clear off'.

clue.text: Want to remove cap by yard? That's crude!

indicators.note: taking the cap off a down entry removes its top letter

parts.note: a dearth is a want or lack

explanation.surface: Someone wants to take off their cap in a yard, and is told that's rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove cap' drops D from DEARTH; 'Want' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and down-to-earth, so crude in the vulgar sense.

clue.text: Endlessly market revolutionary pen like Sappho

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the shortened word is read backwards
without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to sell is to market goods
a Bic is a well-known brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A political radical markets a pen inspired by the poet Sappho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the final L; 'revolutionary' turns the result round. Bic is a ballpoint brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the poet of Lesbos, so lesbic means relating to her island or to lesbian love.

clue.text: Group performing in comeback to make these?

definitions.text: Group performing in comeback to make these?

indicators.note: a comeback returns, so the words are read in reverse

parts.note: a set is a group
on means performing, as an act on stage

explanation.surface: A band performing on its comeback tour produces music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in comeback' reverses SET ON. The whole clue also defines: a performing group makes musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical notes are the sounds a band produces when it plays.

clue.text: Wardrobe man going on about The Equaliser

indicators.note: the theatrical word comes after, going on to the end of the other piece

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a dresser looks after actors' costumes in a theatre wardrobe

explanation.surface: A costume assistant chatters about the TV thriller The Equalizer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Equaliser' looks like the TV show title but is simply one who equalises.
explanation.definitionFit: A redresser sets things right, restoring balance, as an equaliser would.

clue.text: Greek character in charge of a river mouth?

parts.note: delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is put in charge of a river estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta is the fan of land at a river's mouth, so deltaic describes it.

clue.text: Massage one's husband, squeezing black pants

indicators.note: the outer letters squeeze the inner one between them

parts.note: to rub is to massage
one's means one is, I'S, giving IS
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone massages their husband while squeezing his black trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezing' puts B inside the rest. 'pants' is British slang for nonsense, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang 'pants' means worthless nonsense, just like rubbish.

clue.text: Intelligent to get out of head for sure

indicators.note: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: bright means intelligent

explanation.surface: A clever person wants to clear their head, definitely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get out of head' drops the B of BRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Right!' is an interjection of agreement, much like saying 'sure' or 'certainly'.

clue.text: Do you have to get up mornings if you're a punk?

definitions.text: Do you have to get up mornings if you're a punk?

parts.words: Do you have to get up mornings if you're a punk?
parts.note: 'Do' is a hairdo, and the punk's hair has to be got up (spiked upright) every morning

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a question about punks' sleeping habits, but 'Do' is a hairstyle and 'get up' means styling the hair upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mohican is the punk hairstyle with a single upright strip of hair along the scalp.

clue.text: Little drink good? That's not entirely accurate!

parts.note: a half is a half-pint of beer, a small drink in British pubs
right means good, correct

explanation.surface: Someone claims a small drink is good for you, and is told that's dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something half right is only partly correct, hence not wholly accurate.

clue.text: What the latest two pieces from Ono mean to purchasers?

definitions.text: What the latest two pieces from Ono mean to purchasers?

parts.words: What the latest two pieces from Ono mean to purchasers?
parts.note: its last two letters stand for the last two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ono' looks like Yoko Ono, but it is the small-ads abbreviation o.n.o.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller's 'or near offer' tells buyers the asking price is negotiable.

clue.text: Tory figure at polls finally gets in line with others

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a form is a figure or shape

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of polls

explanation.surface: A Conservative candidate at the elections eventually toes the party line.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply with the rules or behaviour of the group.

clue.text: In the past, go around with nurse and Welsh cad

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
a heel is a cad, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: In days gone by, someone went about with a nurse and a Welsh scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the past' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Enwheel is an obsolete verb meaning to encircle or surround.

clue.text: Author is more corny, making lead go west

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is replaced, going over to a different letter

parts.note: triter means more hackneyed or corny

explanation.surface: An author grows more clichéd, sending the protagonist west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making lead go west' swaps the leading T of TRITER for W. 'go west' also means to die, a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is a writer of books or articles.

clue.text: Music producer with leg over a head of Orion

indicators.note: the leg goes over the letter, lying around it

parts.note: pins is slang for legs, so a pin is a leg

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A music producer puts a leg over a head, as if in an odd yoga pose involving Orion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts PIN around A; then O, the head of Orion.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano is an instrument, something that produces music.

clue.text: Trailer engineers look at after prang at the front

indicators.note: the engineers and look come after the first piece
only the front letter of prang is used

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
to view is to look at

explanation.surface: Engineers inspect a trailer after a minor car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prang' is British slang for a minor crash; only its P is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A film trailer is a short preview shown to advertise the movie.

clue.text: You might see me with Her Maj around Windsor primarily

definitions.text: You might see me with Her Maj around Windsor primarily

parts.note: and means with, together

indicators.note: around turns the royal letters about

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

indicators.note: primarily takes only the first letter of Windsor

explanation.surface: A royal speaks: you may see me with the Queen around Windsor.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes Prince Andrew, seen with his mother the Queen at Windsor; 'around' turns the royal cipher about.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew, a son of Queen Elizabeth II of the House of Windsor, would be seen with her.

clue.text: Recent naughtiness ultimately needing reporting

parts.note: new means recent
a sin is a piece of wrongdoing or naughtiness

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of needing

explanation.surface: Recent misbehaviour eventually needs reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsing is an obsolete word for reporting or telling news.

clue.text: Wife men sent up? No good and immoral!

indicators.note: in a down entry, sent up means read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A wife's men were mocked; that's no good and wicked!
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses OR to RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong means morally bad, unethical.

clue.text: Sorrow after female's left? Head to great barman!

indicators.note: the female has left, so her letter is gone from the word

parts.note: grief is sorrow
F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Grieving after a woman walks out, someone heads to a great bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' drops F from GRIEF. 'barman' is not a bartender: a composer works in musical bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Grieg, the Norwegian composer, wrote music in bars, so is a playful 'bar man'.

clue.text: Quickly list rules at first, then strip lacking priest

indicators.note: the first letter of rules is taken
the word is missing the abbreviation for priest

parts.note: to peel off is to strip clothes off

explanation.surface: Rules first, then a striptease without the clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops P from PEEL OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel off is to recite a series of things rapidly and fluently.

clue.text: Preening old fools soon to be trading again?

indicators.note: to fool with something is to play about, so these letters are messed around

explanation.surface: Vain old fools preen themselves, soon to be back in business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fools' is a verb here, rearranging PREENING plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop that is reopening is about to start doing business again after closing.

clue.text: Certain to have hot fellow over end of chair

parts.note: in means fashionable, hot
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to get a handsome man seated over the back of a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in for something is to be bound to experience it, as in 'in for a shock'.

clue.text: Having taken top off, heartily drinks syrups

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: swigs means takes big hearty drinks

explanation.surface: Someone takes their top off and gulps down syrups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'syrups' is rhyming slang: syrup of figs = wigs. 'Having taken top off' drops S.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a syrup (of figs) is a wig.

clue.text: A crowd with a reservation to see some pottery

parts.note: a gate is the crowd attending a sports match

explanation.surface: A crowd with booked seats comes to see a ceramics exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gate' is the size of a sports crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Agateware is pottery with veined colours imitating agate stone.
